documents: Visa copy, plus stamped I-94 for non-residents if applicable
Supplemental declaration for unaccompanied household effects
Detailed inventory in English, with no 'miscellaneous' entries
Power of attorney for your customs broker
Ocean bill of lading or air waybill in your own name
dutyFree: Used household goods you owned and used abroad for at least 1 year
Antiques 100+ years old, or art owned 1+ year for personal use
Silverware and ornaments shipped with normal household goods
restricted: Items owned under 1 year must be listed separately and may pay duty
Vehicles need broker approval first; non-US-standard vehicles shouldn't be shipped
Firearms need an ATF import permit first and must ship separately
Plants, seeds, ivory and pornography are banned; food is discouraged and needs FDA notice
Alcohol is discouraged: some states ban it, others require permits and duty
notes: You must be in the US by the time your goods arrive
An ISF filing is needed at least 24 hours before the ship loads
Shipping papers must name you, not the moving agent, as the receiver
Prescription medicines are fine with a doctor's prescription, up to 3-6 months' supply

documents: EIN number if you hold a US passport (not needed for air)
For a car: original vehicle title with no loan on it
For a financed car: notarised export approval letter from the lender
Power of attorney, depending on the port (mainly for cars)
restricted: Vehicles can only be exported with the original, lien-free title
A car with an outstanding loan needs the lender's written, notarised consent
notes: Requirements vary by port, so check with US Customs at your departure port
